subject: Pricing framework and savings scenarios for inference (batching / KV-cache / quantization)

Subject: Request: Pricing framework and cost scenarios for inference savings

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — we appreciated seeing Redwood's runtime handling high-concurrency chat loads. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask: can you share a pricing framework and 2–3 cost scenarios showing how batching, KV-cache and quantization would impact our monthly spend?

Quick context: Finova runs three primary workloads — customer chat (low latency), statement parsing (batch inference, high throughput), and nightly reranking (very high token volume). Attached is our anonymized usage export (finova_usage_v1.csv).

We'd like: 
- A short spreadsheet with three scenarios (baseline: FP16, mid: mixed quant/batch, high-efficiency: aggressive quant + cache) and estimated cost delta.
- Recommendations on which quant levels and cache policies you’d advise for each workload and the expected quality tradeoffs.
- Any commercial structures you recommend (commits, efficiency credits, pilot pricing).

Timing: procurement is aiming for an internal review on Monday (7/5). Could you get something over by EOD Friday PST?

Thanks,
Sara

Head of Platform Engineering | Finova
[sara@finova.com]

Hi Sara — thanks for the export and clear asks. I put together a short framework and worked examples attached (redwood_pricing_framework_v1.pdf + scenario_breakdown.xlsx). High level summary below so procurement has something in-hand quickly: 

1) Pricing architecture (three levers)
   - Base usage (per-token FP16) — predictable unit price for unoptimized runs.
   - Efficiency credits — earned by hitting caching / batching thresholds (applies as credits against token usage).
   - Quantization uplift tiers — pricing delta for supported quantized variants (we price quantized model variants ~10–25% lower per-token depending on latency/quality SLAs).

2) Scenario sketches (estimates for Finova's usage):
   - Baseline (no cache, FP16): monthly spend = $X (see sheet)
   - Mid (KV-cache enabled with 40–60% prefix hit; batching with 2–4x effective throughput; mixed 8-bit quant on non-latency paths): ~25–40% savings vs baseline.
   - High-eff (aggressive 4-bit quant for nightly jobs + 75% KV-cache hit on chat templates): up to ~55% savings (but requires acceptance testing on quality-sensitive flows).

3) Technical recommendations
   - Chat (low latency): enable small KV-cache for templates, 8-bit dynamic quantization for heavier prompts only, keep decoding paths optimized (prefer 8-bit QAT if you need predictable latency).
   - Statement parsing (batch): push to 4-bit quantized endpoints + large batch windows; use asynchronous batch workers and bulk KV initialization.
   - Reranking (massive token volume): full quantized pipeline + persistent KV-cache; recommend nightly warm-up jobs to pre-populate cache.

4) Commercial playbook
   - 3-month pilot: fixed credits + success metrics (latency, accuracy delta tolerance).
   - 12-month commit: discount band of 10–15% plus efficiency credits unlocking at 60% cache hit.
   - Add-on: Paid model onboarding for 4-bit quantization, or we can do a joint engineering engagement at a time-and-materials rate.

Next steps: if this aligns, I can schedule a 60-minute workshop with your infra and data-science teams to walk the scenario sheet and propose measurable quality gates.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Rachel / team — quick technical note to use in the scenario sheet:

- Quant tradeoffs (empirical): on the family we plan to propose, 8-bit dynamic quantization typically yields ~1.2–1.4x throughput improvement vs FP16 with <1% end-task delta for classification/ranking. 4-bit (QAT where available) can hit ~1.6–2.0x throughput but may increase error rates for generative output by ~0.5–2% depending on prompt sensitivity.
- KV-cache hit assumptions: conservative mid-case 40–60% for customer chat if templates are used; warm-up scripts push this towards 70–80% for predictable dialogs.
- Latency: small-batch, latency-sensitive flows should default to 8-bit. 4-bit is better for large-batch or offline rerank pipelines.
- Model compatibility: not all open checkpoints have 4-bit kernels optimized — for those, we recommend using our 8-bit optimized variant or a model-adaptive approach (switching variants via routing).

I can produce a two-column tech appendix for the spreadsheet (quality delta vs latency numbers) if you want to include measured numbers.

— Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Pricing ops thoughts:

- For a 12-month commit we can offer a 12% list discount (mid-case) + a 5% efficiency credit that vests monthly if KV-cache hit >= 60% and batching throughput >= 2x baseline.
- Pilot: 3 months; provide $10k in usage credits and a one-time model-onboarding credit (covers QAT run and validation).
- We should require a minimum usage floor (to protect economics) — propose $20k/mo absolute minimum for the committed band.

I'll draft a clean offer (MA_Draft_Scope.docx) with the concession bands and suggested SLA language. If Finova pushes on price, we can trade headcount-backed onboarding or a 6-week professional services block instead of deeper discount.

— Priyom
